To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rotation periods of the spotted young stars in the Taurus–Auraniga and Lupus regions are similar to those in other star-forming regions and that the differential rotation is weak in the spotted young stars.
the differential-rotation parameter of the young spotted stars is small and the flares in Lupus 3 were similar to the flares in the Sun.
we found small values of the differential-rotation parameter for three weak-line T Taurus stars, and three flares in the light curve for Lupus 3–14.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of light curves of young stars in star formation regions, which is a first step in the search for planets around these stars.
the rotation of stars in their pre-main-sequence evolutionary phase and the presence of magnetic activity in them.
the following topics: the rotation periods of WTTS, the differential rotation in WTTS, the flares of WTTS and the modulation in CTTS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differential rotation is weak in the studied stars, and that the rotation period is longer than the stellar lifetime, which is a consequence of the slow stellar evolution in young stars.
the rotation of young stars is not yet fully understood, and that the rotation of WTTSs is not necessarily slower than that of classical T Tauris.
the rotation of young stars in the Taurus–Auria and Lupus 2 star-forming regions is not significantly differential, and the stars have no obvious periodic modulation of brightness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the differential-rotation parameter k for WTTSs is small, and the rotation period is not a strong indicator of a WTTS.

the differential-rotation parameter of the stars in the Taurus–Ariuga region is smaller than the one of the stars in other regions, and the stars with the smallest differential-rotation parameter are the WTTSs.

we did not detect any obvious rotational modulation in the WTTS Lupus 3 -14 and RY Tau, while the three WTTS stars V410 Tau, Lupus 3 –48 and V987 Tau show rotational modulation with the differential rotation parameters k of 0.009, 0.0008 and 0.005, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rotation of young stars is not necessarily differential, as is the case with the solar-like rotation of the Sun, and that it can be rigid.
the differential rotation in young stars is weak or even absent, in contrast to the Sun and solar-like stars.

, for the first time, MOST observations of the T Tauri-type stars in the Taurus–Aquila and Lupus regions were obtained and analysed, which allowed us to obtain the values of the solar-like differential-rotation parameters and the flare parameters of the studied stars.
